newsitem.title: USA: Amex says study finds its trades cheaper vs Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: Amex says study finds its trades cheaper vs Nasdaq.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange said a study has concluded that trading costs for institutions on the Amex are cheaper than on the Nasdaq stock market.
The study by Plexus Group, a consultant to institutions and brokerage firms, found that Amex costs were competitive with those of the New York Stock Exchange.

The study, which was funded by the Amex, found that total trading implementation costs, measured as a percentage of the price at the time of the order, were 0.60 percent for the Amex, 0.55 percent for the NYSE, and 1.00 percent on Nasdaq.
Implementation costs measure the net price effect, including commissions, from the time the portfolio manager gives the order to the trading desk to execution.

"This study adds to the growing body of evidence that auction markets provide better executions than dealer markets," said Wayne Wagner, Plexus president. "We've got three studies that say the opposite," a Nasdaq spokesman said. "We are confident that (Nasdaq's) institutional investors receive equal treatment with the Amex."
The study was based on 1995 data from Plexus's database of actual trade executions of more than 40 institutional investment managers.
While the Amex paid for the study, Plexus had already independently collected the data, an Amex spokeswoman said.

Another study, to be published in the Journal of Financial Economics, compares the liquidity of Nasdaq with the NYSE, and concludes that the Big Board is much more able to handle block trades, either without affecting the price of the stock, or with a smaller effect, the New York Times reported on Thursday.
